_comment: Diamond, 1024-atom supercell, LCAO: density of states and AC conductivity from one setup. Both observables reuse the same S^-1/2 preconditioner and the same Chebyshev machinery, so asking for them together costs one setup instead of two. The velocity the AC task needs is the commutator i[H, r] from the model's dipole integrals, so no pseudopotential files are involved. The 1024-atom cell is the primitive cell tiled 8x8x8 at load ('supercell'), with the primitive-cell Hamiltonian folded onto it. An 8x8x8 supercell folds an 8x8x8 primitive-cell k-mesh onto Gamma, so a single k-point already samples the zone densely -- that is what makes the DOS a band spectrum rather than the comb of discrete levels a 4x4x4 cell gives. nsamples is lower than the smaller cell needs because the stochastic trace self-averages: its relative error falls as 1/sqrt(nsamples * dimension), and the dimension is 8x larger here.

run._comment_conv: The 2s2p1d basis puts core-like states near 250 eV, so the Chebyshev expansion spans ~280 eV. The dos task asks for the resolution directly: dE in eV, with the step and moment counts derived from the span at run time -- cost is linear in span/dE, which is why a wide LCAO span makes fine resolution expensive. nsamples controls the stochastic-trace noise, which shows up as negative excursions in derived quantities like the absorption coefficient if it is too small.
run._comment_sparsity: Preconditioner left at defaults deliberately, and this was measured rather than assumed (2026-08: three routes on this system, dos nt=100): (1) raising sptol to 1e-4 does NOT keep S^-1/2 sparse -- density still hits 1.0 after one Newton-Schulz step, so the looser tolerances only bought a cheaper setup (-150s) at the price of Z accuracy 9.5e-4 vs 2.5e-9, and Z is the orthogonalization itself, so that error lands in the spectrum (~0.1-0.3 eV at this 280 eV span). (2) Keeping S and using the sparse seed as a PCG preconditioner per matvec (maxiter 0, operator_form solve) is 5.9x slower per matvec (13 CG iterations each). (3) Peak memory (~81 GB) comes from the seed's concurrent dense subgraph batch, identically in every route -- not from the dense S^-1/2 (2.8 GB). So: full-accuracy Z, S released, is both the fastest and the most accurate route on this system.

tasks._comment: mu sits in the gap of this basis; 300 K is room temperature. nt sets the frequency resolution of sigma(omega) and n_kpm the sharpness of the Fermi occupation.
